old: How to tell direct and indirect objects apart:\n• Direct Object (DO): The thing or person directly affected. Question: ¿Qué? (What?) or ¿A quién? (Whom?). Pronouns: lo, la, los, las.\n• Indirect Object (IO): The recipient. Question: ¿A quién le...? (To/for whom?). Pronouns: le, les (me, te, nos).
new: You know lo, la, los, las from Unit 12 and le, les from the last lesson. How to tell direct and indirect objects apart:\n• Direct Object (DO): The thing, or the person the verb acts on (*Llamé a Carlos*). Question: ¿Qué? (What?). Pronouns: lo, la, los, las.\n• Indirect Object (IO): The person who receives the thing (*Le di el libro*). It usually comes with a direct object. Pronouns: le, les (me, te, nos).
why: screen presents Unit 12's lo/la/los/las as new, and its own ¿A quién? test fits the direct person (Llamé a Carlos) as well as the indirect one
